claim: For the 256 geometric nodes of the magic-square surface \(V\) in Auel–Singer, arXiv:2609.09351v1, the action of \(\mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb Q(\sqrt2,i)/\mathbb Q)\cong C_2\times C_2\) has exactly \(112\) orbits: \(96\) of size \(2\) and \(16\) of size \(4\). More precisely, the \(128\)-point automorphism orbit of \(p_1\) splits into \(64\) pairs defined over \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt2)\), the \(64\)-point orbit of \(p_3\) into \(32\) pairs defined over \(\mathbb Q(i)\), and the \(64\)-point orbit of \(p_2\) into \(16\) quartets defined over \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt2,i)\); in particular, no node is rational over \(\mathbb Q\).

correctness.rationale: The three coordinate representatives lie in \(K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt2,i)\). Coordinatewise conjugation changes the indicated proper subsets of nonzero coordinates; because the geometric automorphism group is defined over \(\mathbb Q\) and acts transitively on each stated orbit, a Galois element fixing one representative fixes that whole orbit, while a nontrivial sign change of the representative fixes no point in that orbit. Orbit-stabilizer gives 64, 16, and 32 Galois orbits, with 256 total nodes and no orbit of size one.

evidence: The paper states that all 256 nodes are defined over Q(√2,i) and gives the three automorphism-orbit sizes; it does not partition the nodes by their smaller fields of definition.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The present claim is a strict arithmetic refinement of the geometric orbit partition: it determines the stabilizer in Gal(Q(√2,i)/Q) of each of the three node families and counts the resulting Galois orbits. It does not claim the full Picard-lattice Galois module.

evidence: The primary source supplies p1, p2, p3, their orbit sizes, and rational coordinate symmetries. Direct conjugation gives stabilizer orders 2, 1, and 2 for the three orbits.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The stated Galois-orbit counts are not quoted as a theorem in the source. They are obtained by a separate coordinatewise Galois calculation and orbit-stabilizer argument. Because the source data permit reconstruction, the claim is presented narrowly as this explicit arithmetic refinement, not as a new description of the surface or its geometric automorphism group.

evidence: Auel–Singer list the three node representatives and geometric-automorphism orbit sizes 128, 64, 64, but do not state the Galois-orbit decomposition.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The claim is equivalent to the field-of-definition distribution of the three transitive geometric-automorphism orbits. The primary text gives the coordinates needed to compute this distribution, but no equivalent Galois-orbit statement was found in the inspected sections.

evidence: The inspected primary text gives geometric-automorphism orbits of the nodes but no Galois-orbit table or distribution of their smaller fields of definition.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: No matching Galois-orbit table was identified in the bounded searches. This is evidence of limited overlap only, not a proof of novelty; the decisive comparison is the inspected primary text and the explicit finite group calculation.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary source gives geometric-automorphism orbits and a common biquadratic field but does not state the Galois orbit sizes or the distribution of the smaller fields of definition. The finite calculation supplies that arithmetic refinement, which is relevant to the Galois action on exceptional divisor classes.
residual_risks: The calculation refines the source's explicit coordinates, so it is an arithmetic computation from published data rather than an independent geometric construction.
No claim is made about the full Galois representation on the Picard group or any Brauer–Manin obstruction.

source_inspections.assessment: The paper states the three geometric orbit sizes 128, 64, 64 and that the nodes are defined over Q(√2,i), but does not state their Galois-orbit distribution.
source_inspections.evidence: The explicit representatives p1, p2, p3 and orbit sizes appear in §1.3; the group is generated by rational coordinate sign changes and square symmetries in §1.2.
source_inspections.material_read: PDF introduction and §1.2–§1.3, including the automorphism-group argument and explicit node representatives.
source_inspections.method: Compared the listed coordinate representatives with each element of Gal(Q(√2,i)/Q), then used equivariance of the rational automorphism group and orbit-stabilizer.
source_inspections.title: The algebraic geometry of 3×3 magic squares of squares
source_inspections.trigger: The paper describes the singular nodes and their geometric automorphism orbits; the Galois action on those nodes is a natural arithmetic refinement.

value.rationale: The fields of definition of the exceptional curves are a concrete input to the Galois-module and arithmetic analysis of the surface. The source identifies the Galois-module structure of the geometric Picard group as relevant to future Brauer–Manin work; this census gives the exact field-of-definition distribution of all 256 exceptional nodes without claiming to solve that broader problem.
